Subject: PO line-item normalization & Ariba onboarding — EDI/OrderForm alignment

Hi David —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Before we start the vendor registration in Ariba, we want to confirm the expected PO payload fields so our Order Form and EDI mapping match ProHealth's procurement system. Two items we need clarity on:

1) Item coding: do your POs reference a single SKU per line (ProHealthItemCode) or do you send both SKU + internal catalog number in separate fields?
2) Quantity/Unit-of-Measure: are partial quantities allowed (decimal) for certain service items, or do you require whole units only?

I attached a small sample_mapping.csv with how Redwood currently emits order lines (columns: order_id, line_number, sku, description, unit_price, qty, uom, vendor_item_id). Could you share the minimal required fields for Ariba ingestion and any normalized code lists we should map to?

Separately, legal flagged that our MSA references PO acceptance by "electronic acknowledgement" — if Ariba includes an automated acceptance status, we want to ensure the Order Form ties to that acknowledgement field. Im looping in our contracts and onboarding leads to confirm: ccd Kim (legal), Marissa (procurement ops), Jonas (platform).

Goal: finish vendor registration + Order Form redline and have a signed Order Form before we get EDI turned on. Can you confirm timeline for provisioning a test vendor in your Ariba sandbox (preferred) and the contact for your EDI team?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Hi Jasmine,

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers up front:

- We use ProHealthItemCode as the authoritative SKU on PO lines. There is an optional vendor_item_id field but it is not required for PO routing.
- Quantity can be decimal for certain contract services (we use 2 decimal places).
- Required fields for Ariba ingestion: PO_Number, PO_Line_Number, ProHealthItemCode, Quantity, UoM, UnitPrice, BillTo_Address_ID, ShipTo_Address_ID.

I attached our vendor_requirements.pdf which includes the Ariba field map and the sample EDI 850/810 segment expectations. For sandbox onboarding, we can create a test vendor account if you provide a vendor contact email and the tax/legal entity name. Expect 2-3 business days for sandbox activation.

EDI contact: ariba-ops@prohealth.com (ccd). They handle the EDI endpoint handshake and GL code mapping.

I'll review the MSA language with Procurement Counsel and flag anything that would block onboarding from our side.

Cheers,
David Owens
Senior Procurement Manager | ProHealth Systems
david.owens@prohealth.com

Jasmine — thanks for the context and the redline. Quick legal read: the current MSA language states that acceptance occurs upon "receipt of an electronic acknowledgement" but doesn't define which acknowledgement maps to the Order Form. Two points:

1) We should clarify that an Ariba "ACK" with status ACCEPTED and a PO_Number referenced shall constitute acceptance for Order Forms only when the Order Form itself references the same PO_Number. That prevents a generic acknowledgement from unintentionally binding terms.

2) Add a short definition in the Order Form: "ProHealthItemCode (external_sku): the unique item code used by the buyer on purchase orders; where provided it will be used for order matching and billing reconciliation."

Ive attached a suggested 2-paragraph addition (I can incorporate into orderform_v2.pdf) and will mark the MSA excerpt with a comment for the legal redline. Operationally, we should avoid extensive contract edits — this is a narrow addendum to the Order Form and an acknowledgement mapping clause.

Marissa: if you can provide the vendor contact, Kim will produce the short addendum and we can push the Order Form to signature (DocuSign link to follow). Jonas, flag if the platform changes are non-trivial.

-kim
